subject: maths
prompt_en: Two straight lines are 4 cm apart at the left edge of a page and 3 cm apart at the right edge. Predict: if the page went on to the right, would they meet?
prompt_hi: Do seedhi lines page ke baayein kinaare par 4 cm door hain aur daayein kinaare par 3 cm. Andaaza lagao: agar page daayi taraf aage badhe, toh kya woh milengi?
answer: Yes: the gap is shrinking, so far enough to the right they meet; they are not parallel

subject: maths
prompt_en: Compare two ruled lines in a notebook with two lines that start 2 cm apart and end 1 cm apart. Neither pair touches on the page. Which pair is parallel, and how can you tell?
prompt_hi: Notebook ki do ruled lines ko un do lines se compare karo jo 2 cm door se shuru hokar 1 cm door khatam hoti hain. Koi bhi page par nahi milti. Kaunsa joda parallel hai, aur kaise pata?
answer: The ruled lines: their gap stays the same. The other pair's gap shrinks, so they would meet

subject: maths
prompt_en: Why can a 2 cm segment and a 10 cm segment still be parallel?
prompt_hi: Ek 2 cm ka segment aur ek 10 cm ka segment phir bhi parallel kyun ho sakte hain?
answer: Parallel is about direction: extended, they never meet and keep the same gap; length has nothing to do with it

subject: maths
prompt_en: Aisha says two crossing lines are not perpendicular because 'neither of them stands straight up', even though the angle is 90°. Is she right?
prompt_hi: Aisha kehti hai do kaatti lines perpendicular nahi hain 'kyunki koi bhi seedhi khadi nahi hai', jabki angle 90° hai. Kya woh sahi hai?
answer: No: perpendicular only needs a 90° angle; the lines can be tilted any way

subject: maths
prompt_en: Kiran says the edge of a book and a pencil lying along it are not parallel because the pencil is shorter. Check his reason.
prompt_hi: Kiran kehta hai ki kitaab ka kinaara aur uske saath rakhi pencil parallel nahi hain kyunki pencil chhoti hai. Uska kaaran check karo.
answer: Wrong reason: length doesn't matter; if they go in the same direction with the same gap, they are parallel

subject: maths
prompt_en: How can you check, using a set-square or a folded paper corner, whether two lines on a page are perpendicular?
prompt_hi: Set-square ya mode hue kaagaz ke kone se kaise check karoge ki page par do lines perpendicular hain ya nahi?
answer: Put the right-angle corner at the crossing; if both lines lie along its two edges, the angle is 90°

subject: maths
prompt_en: A carpenter wants two bookshelves to be parallel. The gap between them is 30 cm at the left end and 31.5 cm at the right end. Are they parallel? What should he fix?
prompt_hi: Ek badhai do shelf parallel lagana chahta hai. Unke beech ka gap baayein 30 cm aur daayein 31.5 cm hai. Kya woh parallel hain? Use kya theek karna chahiye?
answer: No: the gap is not the same everywhere; he should raise or lower one end until both gaps are equal (e.g. 30 cm)

subject: maths
prompt_en: Fold a sheet of paper once, then fold it again so the first crease lies on top of itself. Describe the two creases when you open it.
prompt_hi: Ek kaagaz ko ek baar modo, phir aise modo ki pehli crease khud par aa jaaye. Kholne par dono creases kaise dikhti hain?
answer: They are perpendicular: the second fold makes four right angles where the creases cross

subject: maths
prompt_en: Teach a friend three ways to tell whether two lines are parallel.
prompt_hi: Dost ko 3 tareeke sikhao jinse pata chale ki do lines parallel hain.
answer: Same direction; they never meet when extended; the gap measured at two places is equal (also: a crossing line makes equal corresponding angles)

subject: maths
prompt_en: From memory: if two lines are perpendicular, what are all four angles at their crossing?
prompt_hi: Yaad se: agar do lines perpendicular hain, toh crossing ke chaaron angle kitne hain?
answer: 90° each

subject: maths
prompt_en: Two parallel lines are cut by a transversal. One corresponding angle is 65°. What is the other?
prompt_hi: Do parallel lines ko transversal kaatti hai. Ek corresponding angle 65° hai. Doosra kitna hai?

subject: maths
prompt_en: Two parallel lines are cut by a transversal. One alternate angle is 48°. Find the other alternate angle and the angle that forms a linear pair with it.
prompt_hi: Do parallel lines ko transversal kaatti hai. Ek alternate angle 48° hai. Doosra alternate angle aur uske saath linear pair wala angle nikaalo.
answer: 48°; its linear-pair neighbour is 132°

subject: maths
prompt_en: Two lines are cut by a transversal. The corresponding angles are 75° and 80°. Predict: are the lines parallel? If extended, will they meet?
prompt_hi: Do lines ko ek transversal kaatti hai. Corresponding angles 75° aur 80° hain. Andaaza lagao: kya lines parallel hain? Badhaane par milengi?
answer: Not parallel: the corresponding angles differ (75° ≠ 80°), so extended they will meet

subject: maths
prompt_en: Compare corresponding angles and alternate angles. Where is each pair placed?
prompt_hi: Corresponding angles aur alternate angles ko compare karo. Har joda kahan hota hai?
answer: Corresponding: the same position at each crossing (like both top-left), an F shape. Alternate: between the lines on opposite sides of the transversal, a Z shape

subject: maths
prompt_en: Why are alternate angles equal when the lines are parallel? Use corresponding and vertically opposite angles.
prompt_hi: Parallel lines ke liye alternate angles barabar kyun hote hain? Corresponding aur vertically opposite angles se samjhao.
answer: An alternate angle equals the angle vertically opposite it, which is the corresponding angle of the other alternate angle; corresponding angles are equal for parallel lines, so the alternate angles are equal

subject: maths
prompt_en: Varun drew two lines that clearly meet, crossed them with a transversal, and wrote both corresponding angles as 70° 'because corresponding angles are always equal'. What is wrong?
prompt_hi: Varun ne do lines banayi jo saaf milti hain, unhe ek transversal se kaata, aur dono corresponding angles 70° likhe 'kyunki corresponding angles hamesha barabar hote hain'. Galti kya hai?
answer: They are equal only when the lines are parallel; his lines meet, so the corresponding angles must be different and he should measure them

subject: maths
prompt_en: Lata says two co-interior angles between parallel lines are both 65°. Check her.
prompt_hi: Lata kehti hai parallel lines ke beech do co-interior angles dono 65° hain. Use check karo.
answer: Wrong: co-interior angles add to 180°, so if one is 65° the other is 115°

subject: maths
prompt_en: A road crosses two canals. At the first canal the road makes 112° with the bank; at the second canal the corresponding angle is also 112°. Are the canals parallel?
prompt_hi: Ek sadak do nahron ko kaatti hai. Pehli nahar ke kinaare se sadak 112° banati hai; doosri nahar par corresponding angle bhi 112° hai. Kya nahrein parallel hain?
answer: Yes: equal corresponding angles mean the lines are parallel

subject: maths
prompt_en: On a gate, two straight bars are crossed by a slanting bar. The interior angles on the same side are 50° and 130°. Are the two bars parallel?
prompt_hi: Ek gate par do seedhe bars ko ek tirchha bar kaatta hai. Usi taraf ke interior angles 50° aur 130° hain. Kya dono bars parallel hain?
answer: Yes: the interior angles on the same side add to 180° (50° + 130°), which happens only when the bars are parallel

subject: maths
prompt_en: Trace the letter F and the letter Z over a transversal diagram. Which angle pairs does each letter show?
prompt_hi: Transversal wale diagram par letter F aur letter Z trace karo. Har letter kaunsa angle ka joda dikhata hai?
answer: F shows corresponding angles (under the two arms of the F); Z shows alternate angles (in the two corners of the Z)

subject: maths
prompt_en: Teach a friend how to find all 8 angles when two parallel lines are cut by a transversal and one angle is 55°.
prompt_hi: Dost ko sikhao ki do parallel lines aur ek transversal mein ek angle 55° ho toh saare 8 angle kaise nikaalte hain.
answer: Vertically opposite gives another 55°, linear pairs give 125°; corresponding angles copy these to the other crossing, so four angles are 55° and four are 125°

subject: maths
prompt_en: From memory: if corresponding angles at the two crossings are equal, what can you say about the two lines?
prompt_hi: Yaad se: agar dono crossings par corresponding angles barabar hain, toh do lines ke baare mein kya keh sakte ho?
answer: They are parallel

subject: maths
prompt_en: Two parallel lines are cut by a transversal. One interior angle is 3x and its co-interior partner is 2x. Find x.
prompt_hi: Do parallel lines ko transversal kaatti hai. Ek interior angle 3x hai aur uska co-interior saathi 2x. x nikaalo.
answer: x = 36, so the angles are 108° and 72°

subject: maths
prompt_en: Is 128 − 59 odd or even?
prompt_hi: 128 − 59 odd hai ya even?
answer: Odd (even − odd)

subject: maths
prompt_en: Is 15 × 23 odd or even?
prompt_hi: 15 × 23 odd hai ya even?
answer: Odd (odd × odd)

subject: maths
prompt_en: Is 13 + 25 + 7 + 41 + 9 odd or even?
prompt_hi: 13 + 25 + 7 + 41 + 9 odd hai ya even?
answer: Odd: five odd numbers make an odd sum (it is 95)

subject: maths
prompt_en: Predict: can you pick 5 odd numbers that add up to 50? Try a few, then explain.
prompt_hi: Andaaza lagao: kya tum 5 odd numbers chun sakte ho jinka jod 50 ho? Kuch try karo, phir samjhao.
answer: No: 5 odd numbers always make an odd total, and 50 is even

subject: maths
prompt_en: Compare odd + odd with odd × odd. Why does one give even and the other odd?
prompt_hi: Odd + odd aur odd × odd ko compare karo. Ek even kyun deta hai aur doosra odd?
answer: Odd + odd: the two leftover ones join into a pair, so even. Odd × odd: an odd number of groups, each with one left over, leaves one leftover unpaired, so odd

subject: maths
prompt_en: Why is odd + odd always even? Use pairs.
prompt_hi: Odd + odd hamesha even kyun hota hai? Jodiyon se samjhao.
answer: Each odd number is pairs plus one extra; the two extras make one more pair, so nothing is left over

subject: maths
prompt_en: Zoya says 3 + 5 + 7 = 14. Without adding, how can you tell she made a mistake?
prompt_hi: Zoya kehti hai 3 + 5 + 7 = 14. Bina jode kaise pata chalega ki galti hui?
answer: Three odd numbers must add to an odd number, and 14 is even (the real sum is 15)

subject: maths
prompt_en: A class of 31 students must work in pairs for a project. Can everyone be in a pair with nobody left over?
prompt_hi: 31 bachchon ki class ko project ke liye jodiyon mein kaam karna hai. Kya sab jodiyon mein aa sakte hain bina kisi ke bache?
answer: No: 31 is odd, so one student is always left over (one group would need 3)

subject: maths
prompt_en: Can 5 friends shake hands so that each one shakes hands with exactly 3 others?
prompt_hi: Kya 5 dost aise haath mila sakte hain ki har ek theek 3 logon se haath milaaye?
answer: No: that needs 5 × 3 = 15 'hands', but every handshake uses 2 hands, so the total must be even

subject: maths
prompt_en: Show 7 + 9 with dots in pairs (draw or describe) to explain whether the sum is odd or even.
prompt_hi: 7 + 9 ko jodiyon wale dots se dikhao (banao ya batao) aur samjhao ki jod odd hai ya even.
answer: 7 is 3 pairs and 1 extra, 9 is 4 pairs and 1 extra; the two extras make a pair: 8 pairs, 16, even

subject: maths
prompt_en: Teach a friend how parity proves that 4 odd numbers can never add up to 25.
prompt_hi: Dost ko sikhao ki parity se kaise sabit hota hai ki 4 odd numbers ka jod kabhi 25 nahi ho sakta.
answer: Pair the odd numbers: each pair of odds makes even, so 4 odds = even + even = even; 25 is odd, so it is impossible

subject: maths
prompt_en: From memory: odd + even is odd or even?
prompt_hi: Yaad se: odd + even, odd hota hai ya even?
answer: Odd

subject: maths
prompt_en: Is 2 × 3 × 5 × 7 odd or even?
prompt_hi: 2 × 3 × 5 × 7 odd hai ya even?
answer: Even, because one factor is 2

subject: maths
prompt_en: What is the magic sum of a 3 × 3 magic square that uses 1 to 9?
prompt_hi: 1 se 9 tak wale 3 × 3 magic square ka magic sum kya hai?

subject: maths
prompt_en: Complete the magic square with sum 15. Top row: 8 _ 6; middle row: _ 5 _; bottom row: _ 9 _.
prompt_hi: Sum 15 wala magic square poora karo. Upar: 8 _ 6; beech: _ 5 _; neeche: _ 9 _.

subject: maths
prompt_en: Predict: if you add 10 to every number in the 1-9 magic square, will it still be magic? What will the new sum be?
prompt_hi: Andaaza lagao: 1-9 wale magic square ke har number mein 10 jodne par kya woh magic rahega? Naya sum kya hoga?
answer: Yes: each line has 3 numbers, so every line goes up by 30 and the new sum is 45

subject: maths
prompt_en: Grid A: all rows add to 15, but its columns add to 12, 15 and 18. Grid B: all rows, columns and diagonals add to 15. Which is magic, and why?
prompt_hi: Grid A: saari rows 15 hain, par columns 12, 15 aur 18. Grid B: saari rows, columns aur diagonals 15. Kaunsa magic hai, aur kyun?
answer: Only B: a magic square needs every row, every column and both diagonals to be equal
